newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha firm, end-users quiet on high stocks.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha firm, end-users quiet on high stocks.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha was firmer in afternoon trade on Thursday, but upward momentum was weak compared to sharp overnight gains in crude, traders said.
"Naphtha could have risen as much as $3.00 per tonne given the firmness in crude, but weak fundamentals limited naphtha's gains," one trader said.
He said the regional supply/demand equation was still in the buyers' favour.
Bids for second-half August open-spec naphtha were heard at $198.00 per tonne against offers at about $200.00. It was sold at $198.00 to a Japanese trading house on Wednesday.
In physical naphtha trading, a lack of extra storage capacity kept some Japanese petrochemical firms away from the market, traders said.
Storage facilities are almost full as naphtha suppliers started delivering cargoes at the earliest possible timing ever since near-term spreads turned into contango, they said.

Higher domestic naphtha production also squeezed their storage capacity, they added. Japan produced 1.3 million kl of naphtha in May, up 19 percent from the same period a year earlier, according to the latest trade ministry data.
